Transform Matter. Improve Lives. Shape the Future.
Chemical engineers combine chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, computing and
engineering design to solve problems that matter. They develop cleaner energy systems,
safer manufacturing processes, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, food products,
medical technologies and new ways to protect the environment.
Chemical engineering is one of the most versatile engineering fields, with graduates
working in industries that shape everyday life: chemical manufacturing, biotechnology, energy,
environmental protection, food and consumer products, advanced materials, nuclear
technology, pharmaceuticals, and sustainable manufacturing.
Undergraduate Programs
At Tennessee Tech, chemical engineering students learn by doing. The Department of
Chemical Engineering offers a Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering, a core
undergraduate program with three optional concentrations that combines a strong technical
foundation with hands-on laboratory work, design projects, undergraduate research,
co-ops and internships, and close interaction with faculty. Graduates are prepared
to contribute immediately in industry, continue into graduate school, or pursue professional
pathways such as medicine, law, business or entrepreneurship.
Bachelor of Science, Chemical Engineering:
» Biomolecular Engineering Concentration
Biomolecular Engineering combines knowledge of biological processes and chemical engineering
knowledge. Students interested in biological areas of chemical engineering, such as
medicine, pharmaceuticals, biofuels, bio-remediation, etc., should consider enrolling
in this concentration.
» Chemical Process Manufacturing Concentration
Chemical Process Manufacturing teaches how to turn raw materials into valuable products
through processes that are efficient, safe, and sustainable. But this program goes
beyond traditional manufacturing. You'll explore cutting-edge technologies like cybersecurity
in production, blockchain for supply chains, and remote process control. You’ll also
dive into Industry 4.0, agile manufacturing, Six Sigma, and advanced analytical chemistry—tools
and methods that are transforming the future of manufacturing.
» Energy and the Environment Concentration
Energy and the Environment teaches students ways to protect the environment, support
economic prosperity across society, safeguard human health, and overcome the challenges
facing use of batteries for electric cars, nuclear fuel production and shipping, solar
sourcing, biomass-derived fuels and the reimagining of wastes as resources. You will
learn all aspects of the coming global transition to greener energy.
LEARN MORE
Ready For What Comes Next.
Tennessee Tech’s chemical engineering program emphasizes practical experience. Students
build confidence through laboratory courses, team-based projects, senior design, research
experiences, student organizations, and opportunities to connect with employers through
internships and co-ops.
Our graduates have gone on to work with employers such as Eastman, BASF, DENSO, Cummins
Filtration, Chemours, BWXT, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Y-12, General Electric,
Advanced Composites, Kellogg’s, Tempur-Pedic, the United States Navy and many others.
A Community for Future Engineers.
Chemical engineering students at Tennessee Tech are part of an active and supportive
department community. Through organizations such as the American Institute of Chemical
Engineers student chapter, students develop leadership skills, build professional
networks, participate in service activities, and connect with classmates, faculty,
alumni and industry partners.
Whether your goal is to design better products, improve energy systems, protect the
environment, advance health technologies, or create the next generation of materials,
chemical engineering at Tennessee Tech can help you get there.
